name: probes
description: Benign, non-destructive checks: single safe requests that flag a real exposure only when it is actually present.
author: Plonix

tactics.title: Exposed .git/config
tactics.description: The version-control directory is reachable over HTTP, which can leak source code and history.
tactics.remediation: Block access to the .git directory at the web server or move the working tree out of the web root.

tactics.title: Exposed .env file
tactics.description: An environment file is reachable over HTTP and may contain secrets.
tactics.remediation: Serve application files only; deny access to dotfiles and move secrets out of the web root.

tactics.title: Apache server-status exposed
tactics.description: The server-status page is reachable and discloses request and client information.
tactics.remediation: Restrict mod_status to localhost or trusted networks.

tactics.title: Parameter reflected in response
tactics.description: A request parameter is echoed back in the response body. Reflection is not itself a vulnerability, but it is where output-encoding issues show up, so the endpoint is worth reviewing. The probe value is a harmless marker.
tactics.remediation: Contextually encode any user input that is written into a response.
